# Story 05 — Agent Dashboard

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 completed: project init and structure (see `.squad/plans/checkout/01-*.md`).
- Story 02 completed: customer management — models, services, and routes in `backend/app/models/customer.py`, `backend/app/services/customers.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/customers.py`; frontend pages `frontend/src/pages/CustomersListPage.tsx`, `CustomerDetailPage.tsx`.
- Story 03 completed: ticket management — models, services, and routes in `backend/app/models/ticket.py`, `backend/app/services/tickets.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/tickets.py`; assignment concept (`assignee_id` / assigned agent) already present.
- Story 04 completed: communication channels — see `backend/app/services/channels/`, `backend/app/api/routes/channels.py`, and message send flow (`MessagesPanel.tsx`). Quick-reply insertion will hook into that panel.
- Coordinate with owners of `tickets` (queue/assignment semantics) and `channels` (message send DTOs) before altering shared contracts.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce an **Agent Dashboard** landing experience for the currently active agent. The dashboard is the single screen an agent opens at the start of a shift and shows:

1. **Assigned tickets** — the queue of open tickets currently assigned to the agent, sorted by SLA / priority.
2. **Customer information** — a compact "customer of active ticket" and a "recent customers I've helped" snapshot.
3. **Tasks and reminders** — a personal to-do list scoped to the agent (create / complete / snooze, with optional `remind_at`).
4. **Quick replies** — a manageable library of reusable canned responses (agent-scoped + team-scoped) that can be inserted into a ticket message composer.
5. **Team collaboration** — an @-mentionable **internal note** thread on a ticket plus a lightweight presence / activity feed of teammates ("Sara replied to #123", "Omar took #145").

**Out of scope**

- Full authentication / SSO. Story assumes a lightweight `agents` table and an `X-Agent-Id` header (or similar) already introduced here; real auth is a follow-up.
- Real-time WebSocket delivery. The collaboration feed and presence use short-poll (`GET` refresh every N seconds); a Redis/WS layer is deferred.
- Analytics/reporting dashboards (handled by a later story).

## Product rules (from story)

- **Assigned tickets** — a ticket is "in my queue" when `assignee_id == current_agent_id` and its status is any open/in-progress state (i.e. **not** `closed` / `resolved`). Sort: `priority DESC, due_at ASC NULLS LAST, updated_at DESC`.
- **Tasks and reminders** — an agent-owned entity, independent of tickets, but **optionally linked** to a ticket and/or customer. States: `open` → `done`. Optional `remind_at` timestamp. Only the owning agent sees their tasks.
- **Quick replies** — two scopes: `scope = 'personal'` (owner = an agent) and `scope = 'team'` (owner = null, visible to all agents). Body is plain text with `{{customer.first_name}}` / `{{ticket.id}}` **template tokens** rendered client-side at insert time. Do **not** persist rendered output; store the template.
- **Team collaboration** — two pieces:
  1. **Internal notes on a ticket** — a message with `is_internal = true`; never delivered to the customer channel driver.
  2. **Activity feed** — a lightweight append-only log of events: `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.status_changed`, `ticket.replied`, `note.added`. Scope of what the dashboard shows: last 50 events across tickets the agent is on **or** was mentioned in.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Data model: agents, tasks, quick replies, activity events

**Create file:** `backend/alembic/versions/0004_agent_dashboard.py`. Follow the `op.create_table` / downgrade pattern in `0003_communication_channels.py`.

Tables:

- `agents`
  - `id` (uuid or int, matching id style used by `customers` / `tickets` — verify in `backend/app/models/customer.py` before choosing).
  - `email` (unique, not null).
  - `display_name` (not null).
  - `is_active` (bool, default true).
  - `created_at`, `updated_at`.

- `agent_tasks`
  - `id`, `agent_id` (FK → `agents.id`, indexed, not null).
  - `title` (not null, ≤ 200 chars).
  - `notes` (text, nullable).
  - `status` (enum: `open`, `done`, default `open`).
  - `remind_at` (timestamptz, nullable, indexed).
  - `ticket_id` (FK → `tickets.id`, nullable).
  - `customer_id` (FK → `customers.id`, nullable).
  - `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at` (nullable).

- `quick_replies`
  - `id`.
  - `scope` (enum: `personal`, `team`, not null).
  - `owner_agent_id` (FK → `agents.id`, nullable; **must** be non-null when `scope='personal'`, must be null when `scope='team'` — enforce with a CHECK constraint).
  - `shortcut` (short slug, ≤ 40 chars, nullable, indexed together with `owner_agent_id`).
  - `title` (not null).
  - `body` (text, not null).
  - `created_at`, `updated_at`.

- `activity_events`
  - `id`, `agent_id` (nullable — actor may be system).
  - `event_type` (string enum: `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.status_changed`, `ticket.replied`, `note.added`, `mention`).
  - `ticket_id` (FK → `tickets.id`, nullable, indexed).
  - `customer_id` (FK → `customers.id`, nullable).
  - `payload` (JSONB, nullable — free-form event details, e.g. previous / new status).
  - `mentions` (JSONB array of agent ids, default `[]`).
  - `created_at` (indexed DESC for recency queries).

Add an optional `is_internal` bool (default `false`) to the existing message table **only if** the grep in step Context 3 shows it doesn't already exist. Otherwise reuse.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing `X-Agent-Id`** — every protected route returns `401` (enforced in `deps.get_current_agent`). Frontend interceptor in `frontend/src/api/client.ts` should redirect to a "Pick agent" screen or set the dev default.
- **Agent deleted while session open** — task/quick-reply endpoints return `401`; frontend clears cached agent id.
- **Task links to deleted ticket/customer** — FK `SET NULL` keeps the task; UI renders "(deleted)" placeholder.
- **Quick reply with unknown template token** — token left as literal text; log a `console.warn` in dev.
- **Quick reply scope invariant violated** — DB CHECK rejects; service returns `400` with a specific error message; validated in tests.
- **Internal note accidentally leaks** — enforced by `is_internal=true` in the message insert path bypassing the channel driver; unit-test asserts the driver mock is **not** called.
- **Mention parser** — non-existent `@handle` is silently dropped, not raised, to avoid blocking replies. Tested.
- **Concurrent task completion** — idempotent: completing an already-`done` task returns 200 with unchanged `completed_at`.
- **Polling storm** — `setInterval` cleared on unmount; when the tab is hidden (`document.visibilityState !== 'visible'`), skip the poll.
- **Empty states** — every panel renders a distinct empty state; no infinite spinners.
- **Timezone** — `remind_at`, `due_at`, `created_at` are `timestamptz`; frontend renders in the browser's local zone using existing `formatDate` helper (grep to confirm location) or ISO fallback.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Apply:** `alembic upgrade head` inside `backend/` creates `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `quick_replies`, `activity_events` and (if needed) adds `is_internal` to messages.
- **Seed:** insert one row into `agents` in a small dev-only script (or a note in the README) so `X-Agent-Id: 1` works out of the box.
- **Rollback:** `alembic downgrade -1` drops the four new tables. If the deployment already recorded activity events, capture them beforehand — the downgrade is destructive.
- **Half-applied state:** if migration succeeds but code deploy fails, existing routes are unaffected (all new tables are additive). If code deploys before migration, `/api/dashboard/*` returns 500 on the missing tables — deploy in the order **migration → code**.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt && alembic upgrade head && pytest`.
2. **Backend smoke:** `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`, then:
   - `curl -H 'X-Agent-Id: 1' localhost:8000/api/dashboard/summary`.
   - `curl -H 'X-Agent-Id: 1' localhost:8000/api/dashboard/queue`.
   - `curl -H 'X-Agent-Id: 1' -X POST localhost:8000/api/tasks -d '{"title":"call Ali"}' -H 'content-type: application/json'`.
3. **Frontend runs:** `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev`; visit `/` and confirm redirect to `/dashboard`.
4. **Frontend tests:** `cd frontend && npm test`.
5. **Regression:** `cd backend && pytest -k "not agent"` — pre-existing tests (`test_tickets_crud.py`, `test_channel_messages.py`, etc.) still pass; ticket send path unchanged.
6. **Manual regression:** open a ticket, insert a quick reply into the composer, send — outgoing message body equals the rendered template; add an internal note — customer channel driver **not** invoked.
